angles.idea: Choose the format before the flavour
angles.usefulInsight: A new coffee flavour need not mean a new brewing routine. Start with the format already used at home, then explore the choices within it. The carousel would unfold this decision through a concrete example: Coconut Caramel appears as coffee and single-serve pods, while White Chocolate Pistachio is shown as ground coffee and should not be assumed to have a matching pod. The reader learns to separate flavour curiosity from format availability.

evidence: Warm, toasted pistachios meet sweet white chocolate for a flavor that's earthy, sweet and entirely unapologetic.
hooks: Sweet is only half the description.
White chocolate meets its earthy side.
angles.usefulInsight: For someone considering a dessert-named coffee, the most useful detail is not just the sweet ingredient. White Chocolate Pistachio is described with toasted and earthy notes too. The static would pair the bag prominently with one complete thought: white chocolate names the sweetness; toasted pistachio adds the earthy side of the description. The reader gains a more specific way to judge whether this flavour sounds appealing, without an unsupported promise about sugar, ingredients or intensity.

angles.idea: A coffee bundle can hold two preferences
angles.usefulInsight: A buyer choosing coffee for a shared kitchen can consider a pair of roasts rather than searching for one compromise choice. The supplied range includes Dark Roast + Medium Roast bundles in both bagged coffee and pods. An editorial story would use a clearly hypothetical two-preference household to explain this option, without claiming different people actually prefer those roasts or inventing taste differences or savings.

strategy.imageStyle:
image-0: Wide studio photograph of a dark brown, glossy mug positioned on the right of a pale, grey-veined tabletop. Its handle faces right; a tan circular emblem contains lettering and an antlered animal illustration. A mottled brown glaze descends from the rim. The charcoal background leaves substantial empty space on the left.

image-1: Close, nearly square photograph of the same visible mug design, filling most of the frame. The circular tan emblem, dark curved handle and irregular brown glaze edge are prominent. The setting is a pale veined tabletop against a charcoal wall; highlights reveal the glossy surface. No matching merchandise is visible despite the asset label.

image-2: Upright black coffee bag photographed at a slight angle on a rough, dark surface against a textured charcoal background. Bright green illustrations, cream skull shapes and a white skull-and-crossbones logo contrast with the black packaging. Visible text includes White Chocolate Pistachio and Flavored Ground Coffee. A separate green, black and white Fair Trade Certified badge appears in the lower-left corner. The bag is the dominant focal point.

image-3: A tall black cylindrical container with a black lid and silver-coloured base stands left of a shorter coffee bag. Both carry green and cream illustrations and circular skull-and-crossbones branding. They sit on a pale veined tabletop against a plain dark grey background, with generous space above them.

image-4: A single tall black cylindrical container stands centrally on a pale veined tabletop. Its black lid, silver-coloured base and green-and-cream illustrated upper section are visible against a charcoal background. The composition is spare, with broad negative space on both sides.

image-5: Overhead photograph of four empty clear glasses arranged across a brown wooden board on a pale grey-veined surface. Four dark square panels sit below the glasses. Cream Death Wish Coffee Co. lettering and a small skull-and-crossbones symbol run across the board. The wood grain supplies the main warm colour against the otherwise neutral scene.

Intended direction: Product-led studio imagery with substantial negative space and preserved product proportions. Use the supplied black paper, white ink and red primary/accent roles for typography and surfaces; keep packaging green within the photographs rather than treating it as the brand palette. Follow the declared Revans-Bold heading and Fenomen-Sans-Book body fonts where available, with supplied fallback options otherwise. image-2 is the strongest relevant focal point for the selected flavour story; accessory photographs should not stand in for coffee formats they do not show.
strategy.market: Consumer coffee and coffee accessories sold online. Selling territory and customer geography are unknown.
strategy.mechanism: The supplied collections let shoppers choose coffee by format, roast and named flavour. White Chocolate Pistachio provides a concrete flavour introduction: the website describes warm, toasted pistachios alongside sweet white chocolate, with an earthy and sweet profile. Format availability must be checked for each product rather than assumed across the range.
strategy.note:
This is the pre-post strategy brief; platforms were not specified and no finished posts are included. Audience, restocking trigger and shared-kitchen scenario are creative hypotheses. Geography, customer demographics and purchase motivations are unverified. No taste experience, health effect, caffeine quantity or customer outcome is inferred.

Carousel plan: editorial family, reference IDs S006-04 and S008-17. Use exactly five frames in the later post: introduce changing flavour without changing setup; establish format as the first decision; show Coconut Caramel as a supported cross-format example; explain why format availability cannot be assumed for every flavour; resolve with browsing the collection in the reader's existing format. Prefer a typography-led argument because the supplied photos do not show beans, pods or brewing equipment suitable for an honest format comparison. image-2 may support the ground-coffee example, but should not decorate unrelated comparisons.

Static plan: hero family, reference IDs S008-04 and S008-06. Use image-2 prominently, with a concise headline and the supported earthy/sweet flavour distinction. This is a complete product-specific interpretation, not the carousel opening repeated. Its next action can direct readers to White Chocolate Pistachio in the supplied coffee collection. Reference IDs are planning guidance only; their images were not inspected or treated as assets.

Evidence entries are exact contiguous excerpts from the supplied website text. The supplied sourceUrl remains https://www.deathwishcoffee.com/. The destination is an inspected collection page; no individual product-page URL was supplied. Asset URLs, roles, dimensions and alt text were reviewed alongside the visible images. Several merchandise listings include Sold out, so avoid purchase urgency or accessory-led calls to buy. No current availability beyond the supplied snapshot is verified. For later Instagram posting, a link-in-bio action requires the manual posting guide to set the destination; a LinkedIn caption can include the collection URL directly.

posts.altText: Five-slide guide to choosing a new coffee flavour without changing brewing format. Text-led slides explain starting with ground, whole bean or pods, then show Coconut Caramel as a coffee and pod example. A photograph of the black and green White Chocolate Pistachio ground coffee bag illustrates why each flavour's format should be checked. The closing slide recommends browsing within your existing format.
posts.caption:
Restocking doesn't have to mean repeating yourself. But a flavour name isn't a format: seeing a bag doesn't tell you whether there's a matching pod.

Keep your usual setup as the starting point, then get curious about what goes in it.

On your next order, browse the coffee collection by the format you already use.
posts.emotion: Curiosity without the pressure to reinvent a familiar routine.
